title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; historical weekly sales drop ~14% for 1-day closure in similar grocery product.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 30.5. Thanksgiving (event week) has a historical median lift of x1.12 vs baseline, but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0—insufficient evidence to justify a lift. Price increased 3.4% to $5.20, which historically has not caused a lift (no past promotions at this price). Store closure on Monday reduces demand by ~1/7 (~14%) of weekly sales. No prior promotion at this price point. No evidence of pantry loading. No other drivers. Final adjustment: only closure matters. Median multiplier shrunk toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.5 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 50.3 | 10%-90%: 5.1 - 49.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
